model: REIT AFFO capitalisation at cost of equity (engine route)
model_label: REIT AFFO capitalisation at cost of equity (run on the component engine: revenue x Core FFO margin, less the FFO-to-AFFO bridge (tenant improvements and incentives, maintenance capex, leasing costs, straight-line rent) = AFFO; net debt NOT deducted because FFO/AFFO are already after interest expense and preferred dividends)

inputs.base_revenue_basis: FY2025 (Dec-25 year) total revenue, US$m, per the FY2025 10-K / year-end press release (8-K 2026-02-12 ex-99.1) and FRT_Metrics.csv. Revenue is the DRIVER line only; the flow valued is AFFO, reconstructed as Core FFO less recurring re-leasing and maintenance capital and straight-line rent. FRT introduced long-term 'FFO and AFFO per share' targets at its May-2026 Investor Day but does not publish an AFFO reconciliation in the earnings release, so the bridge here is the house definition applied to the company's own disclosed lines.
inputs.share_count_basis: Weighted average common shares, DILUTED, on the Nareit/Core FFO basis for Q2 2026 (86,803 thousand; Q2 2026 press release FFO reconciliation, 8-K 2026-07-31). This count includes the downREIT operating partnership units and the 5.417% Series 1 convertible preferred, both of which are dilutive for FFO and whose income is added back to (or not deducted from) FFO available to common shareholders -- numerator and denominator are on the same basis. Basic shares issued and outstanding were 86,883,595 at 30-Jun-2026 and 86,889,133 at 27-Jul-2026 (10-Q cover). Held FLAT: FRT issues modest equity through its ATM (US$60.5m in H1 2026, US$54.5m in H1 2025) to fund acquisitions on a leverage-neutral basis, which is growth funding rather than compensation and is captured by using per-share-equivalent growth rates on a flat count (see growth_rationale); SBC (US$14.6m FY2025) is expensed inside FFO, so diluting the count as well would double count.
inputs.net_debt_note: Deliberately ZERO in the model. The flow capitalised is AFFO, which is already AFTER interest expense (US$183.6m FY2025; US$99.1m H1 2026, deducted from net income before FFO is struck) and after preferred dividends (US$7.5m/yr, deducted in 'Nareit FFO available for common shareholders'). Deducting the balance-sheet net debt on top would charge the financing cost twice (dcf-methods SKILL.md: capitalise a post-interest flow at the cost of equity and never subtract net debt). total_debt, cash and net_debt_actual below are recorded for audit and leverage context only.
inputs.total_debt_note: US$m at 30-Jun-2026 (Q2 2026 10-Q balance sheet): mortgages payable, net 518.371 + notes payable, net 1,282.856 (US$286.2m revolver + US$1.0bn unsecured term loans, net of costs) + senior notes and debentures, net 2,966.685 (includes the US$485m 3.25% exchangeable notes due Jan-2029) = 4,767.912. Excludes operating (70.9) and finance (13.0) lease liabilities and the US$159.8m of preferred shares at liquidation preference (150.0 Series C 5.0% + 9.8 Series 1 5.417%). Down from 4,963.6 at 31-Dec-2025 after US$400m of senior notes were repaid in H1 2026, funded by a US$250m term-loan draw (Feb-2026) and disposition proceeds.
inputs.cash_note: US$m at 30-Jun-2026 (Q2 2026 10-Q). Working cash only; FRT has no net-cash position. Recorded for audit, not netted against the AFFO-capitalised value.
inputs.net_debt_actual_note: total_debt less cash at 30-Jun-2026, for leverage context: ~5.4x net debt / EBITDAre per management; fixed-charge coverage 3.9x (Q2 2026 press release). Not used in the valuation.
inputs.last_fcf_note: FY2025 AFFO, US$m, house reconstruction: Core FFO 610.991 less tenant improvements and incentives 80.082 less maintenance capital expenditures 29.362 less leasing costs 23.114 less straight-line rent 27.976 = 450.457 (all lines from the FY2025 year-end press release 'Summary of Capital Expenditures' / 'Other Information' tables and the 10-K cash-flow statement). = US$5.21 per diluted share on 86.498m FY2025 diluted shares; AFFO/Core FFO conversion 73.7%. FY2024 on the same definition: 570.708 - 83.566 - 24.552 - 31.049 - 26.8 = 404.741 (US$4.80/share on 84.286m). Trailing twelve months to 30-Jun-2026: FY2025 450.457 - H1 2025 218.742 + H1 2026 244.290 = 476.005 (US$5.48 per diluted share on 86.803m). This is NOT the CSV FreeCashFlow (blank) and NOT OCF less all capex (OCF 622.4 less 303.2 total capex incl. US$193.7m development/redevelopment = 319.2), because development and redevelopment spend is growth capital funded by dispositions and leverage-neutral equity, not a recurring charge against the existing portfolio's distributable cash flow. In-place lease amortisation (~US$11.8m FY2025 for comparable properties) and above/below-market rent amortisation are not deducted; they are small and partly offsetting.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: FY2025 Core FFO available to common shareholders, US$m (US$7.06 per diluted share) -- Nareit FFO of 624.256 (US$7.22) less US$13.0m of one-time new-market-tax-credit transaction income and US$0.3m of collected COVID-deferred rents. Core FFO is the flow management guides to (FY2026: US$7.48-7.56) and the base for the FFO-margin driver below. Nareit FFO per diluted share history from the year-end press releases: FY2019 6.17, FY2020 4.38 (COVID), FY2021 5.57, FY2022 6.32, FY2023 6.55, FY2024 6.77, FY2025 7.22.
inputs.sbc_source: Share-based compensation (US$14.6m FY2025, US$7.9m H1 2026; press-release 'Other Information' line and cash-flow statement) is expensed inside net income and therefore inside Nareit/Core FFO and AFFO; it is NOT added back anywhere in the bridge, so it is already charged once in the flow being valued. Shares withheld for employee taxes (US$5.0m H1 2026, financing activities) are part of that same charge. No further SBC adjustment is made; house and street bases coincide (SBC-zero convention for the REIT row of the routing table), so band_position is null.
inputs.interest_income_note: Zero. FRT holds working cash only (US$107m against US$4.77bn of debt); there is no net-cash pile whose interest could be double counted.
inputs.buyback_note: No share repurchases in FY2025 or H1 2026; FRT is a modest net ISSUER via its ATM (US$60.5m H1 2026). The flat count is a modelling convention: growth rates are per-share-equivalent (see growth_rationale), so the ATM issuance and the acquisitions it funds net to roughly zero per share.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-09-25T20:00:03Z NYSE regular close (Yahoo v8 chart meta); 52-week range 90.03-128.21
inputs.nta_note: GAAP book value per common share: total shareholders' equity of the Trust 3,364.530 less preferred at liquidation preference 159.822 = 3,204.708 / 86.884m basic shares = US$36.89; on total shareholders' equity incl. preferred = US$38.72. Historical-cost book value under real-estate depreciation (net real estate 8,234.0 after 3,351.9 of accumulated depreciation), NOT a fair-value NTA -- FRT does not carry investment property at IAS-40 fair value. Recorded as a leverage/solvency cross-check only; depreciated cost materially understates the economic value of 60-year-old coastal infill assets such as Santana Row and Bethesda Row.
inputs.core_ffo_fy2026_guidance: 7.48-7.56 (raised and tightened 31-Jul-2026 from 7.46-7.55; initial Feb-2026 range 7.42-7.52); implies 5.9-7.1% Core FFO/share growth; Comparable Property POI growth 3.25-3.75%
inputs.dividend_history_note: Quarterly common dividend raised 3% to US$1.16 (payable 15-Oct-2026), the 59th consecutive annual increase. FY2025 dividends declared US$4.46/share = 62% of Nareit FFO and 86% of house AFFO (US$5.21); at the new US$4.64 run-rate against TTM AFFO of US$5.48 the payout is 85% -- covered, with the residual ~US$70m/yr of retained AFFO plus disposition proceeds and ATM issuance funding the ~US$400m residential densification pipeline. Cross-check only; not a model input.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Discount rate is the USD COST OF EQUITY, not a WACC, because AFFO is a post-interest, post-preferred flow and no net debt is deducted. 10-year US Treasury 5.18% (^TNX, 25-Sep-2026 close) + 1.0 beta x 5.5% US equity risk premium = 10.7%. Beta of 1.0 (below the 1.2 used for office REIT BXP) reflects an A-/Baa1 investment-grade, grocery-anchored and mixed-use portfolio with 96% leased, no tenant above 2.6% of ABR and a 59-year dividend-growth record; interest-rate sensitivity is rated 'moderate-to-high' in the Analysis JSON and is charged through the 5.18% risk-free base rather than a beta premium. The same 10.7% is used in all three scenarios (risk charged once, in the flows). Cross-check: at current_price the market capitalises TTM AFFO/share of US$5.48 at a 5.0% AFFO yield (20.2x) and FY2026E Core FFO of US$7.52 at 14.7x (6.8% FFO yield); the dividend yield is 4.2%. The market is therefore discounting FRT's AFFO stream at roughly 7.5-8% with growth, i.e. it does not demand this model's 10.7% cost of equity from a Dividend King -- the model's discount to price is the price of that gap, not evidence of a broken business.
inputs.lease_treatment: FRT's own lessee obligations (ground leases; US$70.9m operating + US$13.0m finance lease liabilities at 30-Jun-2026) are immaterial relative to US$4.77bn of debt and sit inside FFO/AFFO as an operating expense; not separately modelled and not included in total_debt (consistent with the debt figure's composition, which excludes lease liabilities). lease_cost_pct_path is 0 in every scenario.
inputs.nci_treatment: FFO and AFFO are stated net of noncontrolling interests in consolidated partnerships (net income attributable to NCI, US$12.6m FY2025 / US$4.8m H1 2026, is deducted before FFO is struck; redeemable NCI of US$183.1m and NCI in equity of US$70.0m at 30-Jun-2026 are the matching balance-sheet items). DownREIT operating partnership units are handled the other way: their income (US$2.5m FY2025) is added back to FFO and the units (~0.53m share-equivalents) are included in the diluted share count used here. Charged once, on both sides.
inputs.notes: MODEL: REIT AFFO capitalisation at cost of equity, run through the component engine as revenue x Core FFO margin less an AFFO capital bridge (capex_pct_path), with D&A, SBC, cash tax and working capital all at zero and net_debt at zero -- the same construction used for BXP and consistent with the ARG.NZ / PCT.NZ / IPL.NZ AFFO-at-CoE convention (never subtract net debt from a post-interest flow). WHY: FRT is a US equity REIT (open-air shopping centres and mixed-use, 103 properties, 28.8m sq ft, ~2,500 residential units); GAAP net income (US$423.6m FY2025, US$4.68 EPS) is dominated by gains on sale (US$150.1m FY2025) and real-estate depreciation (US$320.3m) and is not the flow shareholders own; reported OCF less ALL capex conflates recurring re-leasing capital with growth development spend. Fresh build (no prior FRT DCF or Drivers file; no memory entry). ENGINE FIELD MAPPING for the reader: ebitda_margin_path = Core FFO / revenue (FY2025 actual 47.8%, FY2024 47.5%, H1 2026 48.1%); capex_pct_path = FFO-to-AFFO bridge / revenue (FY2025 actual 12.55%, FY2024 13.8%, H1 2026 12.0%); the engine's 'fcf' row is therefore AFFO and 'owner_fcf_margin' is the AFFO margin (FY2025 actual 35.2%). Data sources are SEC XBRL (Metrics.csv) plus the FY2025 and Q2 2026 8-K earnings releases and the Q2 2026 10-Q pulled from EDGAR in this session for the FFO reconciliations, capex summaries, 30-Jun-2026 balance sheet and diluted FFO share count; the DB kpis table carries no FFO series. Price is the Friday 25-Sep-2026 regular close (valuation date is the following Monday); not an after-hours print.

historical_growth.revenue_basis: FY2022 1,074.4 -> FY2025 1,279.0 (3yr) and FY2020 835.5 -> FY2025 1,279.0 (5yr, off the COVID-depressed FY2020 base; FY2019 -> FY2025 is 5.3%/yr). Includes acquisitions (US$735m of real estate bought in FY2025) funded partly by ATM equity, so total revenue growth overstates per-share growth.
historical_growth.eps_basis: Statutory diluted EPS is not used: FY2022 4.71 (US$155m of gains on sale), FY2023 2.80, FY2024 3.42, FY2025 4.68 (US$150m gains, US$13m tax-credit income) -- a series driven by disposition gains and depreciation, not operating performance; the FY2020 base (1.62) is the COVID trough. Core FFO per diluted share is the relevant series: FY2022 6.32 -> FY2025 7.06 = 3.8%/yr (Nareit FFO 6.32 -> 7.22 = 4.5%/yr); pre-COVID FY2019 6.17 -> FY2025 7.22 = 2.7%/yr over six years.
historical_growth.equity_basis: Total shareholders' equity FY2022 3,034.0 -> FY2025 3,319.0 and FY2020 2,548.7 -> FY2025 3,319.0. Book equity for a REIT is depreciated cost and grows mainly through ATM issuance net of the >100% AFFO-to-book distribution; it is not the growth anchor.
historical_growth.fcf_basis: AFFO on the house definition is reconstructed for FY2024 (404.7, US$4.80/share) and FY2025 (450.5, US$5.21/share; +8.5% per share) only -- the older year-end releases were not pulled for the capex tables, so no 3- or 5-year AFFO CAGR is stated. The CSV FreeCashFlow column is blank (XBRL capex untagged) and OCF less total capex would in any case mix growth development spend into the series.
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Core FFO per diluted share 3-year CAGR (3.8-4.5% depending on Nareit vs Core basis), cross-checked against the FY2026 guidance (+6.5% at the midpoint, a year flattered by acquisitions and record leasing) and the 2.7%/yr six-year pre-COVID-to-FY2025 rate. Used as the year-2-to-3 growth anchor in the base case; the terminal rate is 2.5%.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (3.0% / 5.4%) and revenue CAGR (6.0% / 8.9%) diverge by more than 30% on both windows and statutory EPS CAGRs are meaningless (gains-on-sale driven, COVID base); neither is used. The valuation anchors on Core FFO per share and the FFO-to-AFFO bridge instead.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF CAGRs are not the relevant series for a REIT (SKILL.md routing row); AFFO per share is, and only two years are reconstructed. SBC is immaterial (1.1% of revenue) and is expensed inside FFO, so there is no SBC-adjusted vs reported divergence to report.

base.growth_rationale: Y1 (FY2026, +8.0% revenue) lands Core FFO at ~US$652m = US$7.51 per share on the flat 86.803m count, matching the raised US$7.48-7.56 guidance midpoint; H1 2026 revenue was already +9.0% (676.8 vs 620.7) on FY2025 acquisitions, record leasing (TTM 2.8m sq ft at +17% cash / +29% straight-line spreads) and small-shop occupancy at 92.3%. Y2-Y4 (5.0% -> 4.0%) reflect Comparable Property POI growth of ~3.5% plus the ~US$27m of incremental POI from the ~US$400m residential densification pipeline (Willow Grove, Lot 12 Santana Row, The Blair at Ballard + Kenwood, 301 Washington) delivering FY2027-FY2029, plus accretive leverage-neutral recycling; rates are per-share-equivalent on a flat count (ATM issuance and the acquisitions it funds net to ~zero per share). Fades to 3.0% and then 2.5% (contractual escalators ~2-2.5% plus modest rollover spreads) once the current lease-up and development wave is absorbed -- in line with the 2.7%/yr pre-COVID-to-FY2025 FFO/share record and below the 3.8-4.5% 3-year CAGR.
base.margin_rationale: Core FFO margin on revenue. FY2025 actual 47.8% (FY2024 47.5%, H1 2026 48.1%). Y1 set to 47.2% because FY2026 guidance implies Core FFO of ~US$652m on ~US$1,381m of revenue: interest expense is running +14% (H1 2026 99.1 vs 87.1) as the US$452m of 2.0%-coupon 2026 maturities were refinanced with a 4.4%-5% term loan/revolver and the FY2025 acquisitions were partly debt-funded. Recovers only to 47.5% and holds: the US$893m of 2027 maturities (revolver, US$200m Bethesda Row mortgage, notes) reprice from ~3-4% to ~5%, offsetting operating leverage from POI growth. No assumption of a return to the ~48% H1 2026 run-rate.
base.capex_rationale: The FFO-to-AFFO bridge (tenant improvements and incentives + maintenance capex + leasing costs + straight-line rent) as % of revenue: FY2025 actual 12.55%, FY2024 13.8%, H1 2026 12.0%. Held near 12.3% in the near years -- record leasing volume carries record TI/leasing-cost dollars (H1 2026 TI 43.1 vs 42.7; leasing costs 11.7 vs 13.2) -- easing to 12.0% as the straight-line component (US$28m FY2025, inflated by 27-29% straight-line spreads on new leases) normalises once the leasing wave matures. Gives FY2026E AFFO of ~US$482m = US$5.55/share versus TTM actual US$5.48 and FY2025 US$5.21.
base.tax_rationale: Zero: FRT qualifies and elects to be taxed as a REIT and distributes at least 90% of REIT taxable income; cash taxes paid were US$0.4m in FY2025 (TRS-level only). FFO/AFFO are already the after-tax distributable flow.
base.terminal_note: Gordon at 10.7% / 2.5% = 12.5x terminal AFFO (an 8.0% terminal AFFO yield) binds well below the 20x cap. FRT trades at ~20x TTM AFFO today; the model's exit multiple is deliberately not the current one -- the cap is a brake, not a target.

bull.growth_rationale: FY2026 lands at or above the top of guidance (US$7.56+) as Q2 2026 did; the record 2026 leasing volume (819k sq ft signed in Q2 alone at +15% cash / +28% straight-line) commences through FY2027-FY2028 and small-shop occupancy pushes past 93%; the residential pipeline delivers its ~US$27m of POI on schedule; the Fed easing cycle lowers refinancing coupons on the 2027 maturities and reopens accretive acquisitions in the new central markets (Kansas City, Omaha, Denver) at a sub-5% effective cost of capital. Per-share FFO compounds at ~6% through FY2029 -- the upper end of the Investor Day framework -- before fading to 3.0%.
bull.margin_rationale: Core FFO margin expands ~1pp as lower short rates (revolver/term loans at SOFR + 72.5bp, US$1.0bn floating before swaps) and cheaper refinancing of the 2027-2029 maturities let interest expense grow slower than revenue, and as the residential/mixed-use densification adds POI on land already owned (no incremental land cost).
bull.capex_rationale: Re-leasing capital intensity eases toward 11.5% of revenue (H1 2026 was 12.0%) as occupancy stabilises at multi-decade highs, lease terms lengthen and the straight-line component shrinks with maturing spreads.
bull.terminal_note: Gordon at 10.7% / 3.0% = 13.4x terminal AFFO binds below the 22x cap; the bull case does not assume the market's current ~20x AFFO multiple persists at exit.

bear.growth_rationale: FY2026 still lands near the low end of guidance (~US$7.39/share; the year is largely contracted) but growth then stalls: a consumer/tariff-driven slowdown brings a wave of retailer bankruptcies and store closures (the Analysis JSON's tenant-health and consumer-spending risks), small-shop occupancy slips back below 90%, releasing spreads compress from mid-teens to low single digits, and the residential densification pipeline is delayed by entitlement and construction-cost overruns and leases up slowly. Per-share FFO grows only ~1-2%/yr from FY2027 -- roughly the pre-COVID 2016-2019 experience, when FFO/share grew 2-3% despite a benign backdrop -- with no recovery to the base path.
bear.margin_rationale: Core FFO margin compresses ~3pp: the US$893m of 2027 maturities and the US$485m 3.25% exchangeable notes (Jan-2029) refinance at 5.5-6% in a higher-for-longer rate environment (each 1pp on ~US$1.4bn is ~1.1pp of revenue margin), bad-debt expense rises with tenant failures, and property insurance costs in coastal/climate-exposed markets keep climbing faster than reimbursements.
bear.capex_rationale: Re-tenanting vacated anchor and small-shop space after bankruptcies requires larger tenant improvement packages and leasing commissions (FY2024 ran at 13.8% of revenue with a heavier TI/leasing-cost load); the bridge rises to 14.0% of revenue, cutting AFFO conversion of Core FFO to ~69% and pushing the US$4.64 dividend's AFFO payout above 95% by the outer years -- a 59-year dividend-growth streak at risk of stalling, not of a cut.
bear.terminal_note: Gordon at 10.7% / 2.0% = 11.7x terminal AFFO binds just under the 14x cap (an 8.5% exit AFFO yield, consistent with shopping-centre REIT pricing in the 2023 rate-shock trough).

scenario_narratives.base: FRT executes the plan laid out at its May-2026 Investor Day: Core FFO/share lands at the ~US$7.52 guidance midpoint in FY2026 on record leasing and FY2025 acquisitions, then compounds ~4-5%/yr through FY2029 as the ~US$400m residential densification pipeline delivers ~US$27m of POI and comparable POI grows ~3.5%, before fading to 2.5% escalator-driven growth. Interest expense on the 2026-2027 refinancings caps the Core FFO margin near 47.5%, and the FFO-to-AFFO bridge stays at ~12% of revenue, so AFFO/share grows from US$5.21 (FY2025) to ~US$5.55 (FY2026E) and ~US$7.7 by FY2035. The dividend (US$4.64) stays ~85% covered by AFFO. Capitalised at a 10.7% cost of equity the stream is worth materially less than the market's ~20x AFFO multiple implies; the gap is the discount rate, not the business.
scenario_narratives.bull: The leasing supercycle in supply-constrained coastal retail persists: 2026's record volume commences through FY2027-FY2028 at mid-teens cash spreads, small-shop occupancy exceeds 93%, the residential pipeline delivers on time, and a Fed easing cycle lowers refinancing coupons and reopens accretive acquisitions in the new central markets at a sub-5% effective cost of capital. Core FFO/share compounds ~6%/yr through FY2029 (top of the Investor Day framework), the FFO margin expands ~1pp as interest expense lags revenue, and re-leasing capital intensity eases to 11.5% of revenue.
scenario_narratives.bear: A consumer/tariff-driven slowdown brings a wave of retailer bankruptcies; small-shop occupancy slips below 90% and releasing spreads compress to low single digits. Higher-for-longer rates reprice the US$893m of 2027 maturities and the 2029 exchangeable notes at 5.5-6%, compressing the Core FFO margin ~3pp, while re-tenanting vacated space pushes TI and leasing costs to 14% of revenue. FFO/share growth stalls at 1-2% from FY2027, AFFO conversion falls toward 69%, and the dividend payout of AFFO exceeds 95% -- the 59-year growth streak survives only through token increases. Exit at an 8.5% AFFO yield.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear lifted from the house default 15% to 25%: the Analysis JSON rates tenant health, geographic concentration, leverage/refinancing, interest-rate sensitivity and consumer/tariff risk all 'moderate' and the premium P/FFO multiple leaves no cushion for a growth deceleration; US$1.4bn of 2027-2029 debt reprices in a 5%+ ten-year environment. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because the bull case needs three independent things to go right (leasing spreads sustained, on-time pipeline delivery AND a rate-easing cycle), and because FY2026 guidance has already been raised twice -- the easy upgrades are in the base. Base 50%: the year is largely contracted, guidance was raised and tightened, and the balance sheet (A-/Baa1, 5.4x net debt/EBITDAre, 3.9x fixed-charge cover, US$1.4bn revolver to 2030) carries no solvency or dividend-cut risk in any scenario.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Capitalise the distributable cash flow FRT actually produces for common shareholders -- AFFO, i.e. Core FFO after recurring re-leasing capital, maintenance capex and non-cash straight-line rent -- at a USD cost of equity, with no net-debt deduction because the flow is already after interest and preferred dividends. GAAP net income (gains on sale, real-estate depreciation), reported OCF less all capex (which mixes growth development spend into the series) and depreciated-cost book value are each recorded as cross-checks but not valued. The three scenarios vary the leasing/occupancy cycle, the refinancing coupon on 2027-2029 maturities and re-leasing capital intensity; the discount rate is held at 10.7% in all three so risk is charged once, in the flows. The valuation is deliberately more demanding than the market's ~5% AFFO yield: it asks what the stream is worth to an owner requiring an equity return, not what a yield-seeking buyer will pay.
key_risks_to_valuation: The AFFO bridge is a house reconstruction: FRT does not publish an AFFO reconciliation in its earnings release, and the tenant-improvement line it labels 'non-maintenance' is deducted here in full (US$80.1m FY2025). If a material share of that TI is first-generation redevelopment spend, AFFO is understated by up to ~US$0.5/share and every scenario is ~10% too low; if the Investor Day AFFO definition also deducts in-place lease amortisation, it is ~US$0.1/share too high.

Discount-rate sensitivity: at a 10.7% cost of equity the base value sits far below the price, and each 1pp on the rate moves the base value by roughly 12-15% (see the sensitivity grid). The market is capitalising FRT's AFFO at ~7.5-8% with growth; the required_return_table shows what today's price implies.

Refinancing coupon on the US$893m 2027 maturities, the US$1.0bn floating term loans (US$450m swapped to Mar-2028) and the US$485m 3.25% exchangeable notes due Jan-2029 -- each 1pp is ~1pp of FFO margin.
Growth rates are per-share-equivalent on a flat 86.8m diluted count; if ATM issuance (US$60m H1 2026) funds dilutive rather than accretive deployment, per-share growth undershoots the paths.
Development execution on the ~US$400m residential densification pipeline (entitlements, construction cost inflation, lease-up) and the assumed ~US$27m of stabilised POI.
Price is the 25-Sep-2026 regular close; the valuation date is the following Monday. Guidance is as of 31-Jul-2026; Q3 2026 results (early Nov) will refresh it.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance v8 chart API at inputs.price_as_of (NYSE regular close); 52-week range 90.03-128.21.
data_sources.financials: SEC XBRL company facts via FRT_Metrics.csv (revenue, net income, OCF, equity, debt, shares through Q1 2026); FY2025 year-end earnings release (8-K filed 2026-02-12, ex-99.1) and Q2 2026 earnings release (8-K filed 2026-07-31, ex-99.1) for the Nareit/Core FFO reconciliations, capital-expenditure summaries, leasing costs, straight-line rent, dividends, debt maturities and 2026 guidance; Q2 2026 10-Q (filed 2026-07-31) for the 30-Jun-2026 balance sheet, cash-flow statement and diluted share tables; FY2020, FY2022 and FY2024 year-end releases for the FFO/share history; ^TNX via Yahoo for the risk-free rate.
data_sources.qualitative: FRT_Analysis.json (2026-09-28): business model, moat, risks, growth drivers, Q2 2026 developments and guidance, bull/bear cases.
